title: com.github.mnestor.ssoossh
description: Preference Domain: com.github.mnestor.ssoossh, Application: ssoossh client. Every key here is a locked setting: a value delivered this way outranks the user's own ssoossh.yaml and cannot be overridden by them. Omit any key you do not want to enforce -- an omitted key leaves the user's own value in effect, which is not the same as setting it to a default.

server.title: Server URL
server.description: Base URL of the ssoosshd server the client authenticates against, e.g. https://ssh.example.com. Locking this is the usual reason to deploy this profile at all: it stops a client being pointed at another server.

capubkey.title: CA Public Key
capubkey.description: The server's CA public key in authorized_keys form, pinned so the client verifies the CA it was given rather than whichever one the server offers.

insecure_skip_verify.title: Skip TLS Verification
insecure_skip_verify.description: Disables verification of the server's TLS certificate. Turns TLS into obfuscation -- anyone who can redirect the connection can also present their own certificate. Set this false to forbid users turning it on; there is no good reason to push it true outside a lab.

use_agent.title: Use SSH Agent
use_agent.description: Load issued certificates into the running ssh-agent rather than writing them to disk.

fallback_file_agent.title: Fall Back To File Agent
fallback_file_agent.description: When no ssh-agent is reachable, fall back to writing the key and certificate to disk instead of failing.

key_filename.title: Key Filename
key_filename.description: Path the generated keypair and certificate are written to when the file agent is used.

try_open_browser.title: Open Browser Automatically
try_open_browser.description: Open the system browser for the OIDC login rather than only printing the URL.

fips.title: FIPS Mode
fips.description: Restricts key generation to FIPS-approved algorithms. Genuinely three-state: leave it Not Configured to say nothing, which is not the same as Configured-false. With it true, a non-approved SSH Key Type is a hard error at startup rather than a silent downgrade.

sshkey.type.title: SSH Key Type
sshkey.type.description: Key algorithm the client generates. The default is ecdsa (P-384) unconditionally. ed25519 stays selectable but is not FIPS-approved, so it is a hard error when FIPS Mode is on. Note the key name contains a literal dot.

sshkey.size.title: SSH Key Size
sshkey.size.description: Means a different thing per algorithm: for ecdsa it is the NIST curve (256, 384 or 521), for rsa the modulus size in bits (2048 minimum), and nothing at all for ed25519, which has one size. Omit it to take the default for the chosen algorithm. Note the key name contains a literal dot.

forbidden_certificate_extensions.title: Forbidden Certificate Extensions
forbidden_certificate_extensions.description: SSH certificate extensions the client refuses to request, on top of the ones it always subtracts. Each entry is an extension name such as permit-agent-forwarding or permit-port-forwarding.
